messages:
Devon: quick thread — ran a focused perf pass comparing FlashAttention variants (fused vs paged) across prefill and decode paths. seeing a weird tail on small-batch decode (15-30% slower p95) when KV page boundaries hit mid-request.
Maria: can you paste the exact run command + env so I can repro?
Devon: ran on dedicated-gpu-3 with: `GOPS_PROFILE=1 ./run_bench --model=mpt-7b --seq=2048 --mode=prefill_then_decode --microbatch=1-4 --workload=chat` . profiling shows repeated kernel switches between fa_v2_fused and fa_paged during decode.
Sasha: by "page boundary" you mean when kv length crosses the 4096/8192 alignment and we route to paged kernels?
Devon: exactly. when kv_len % 4096 == 0 the router prefers paged variant; continuous batching sometimes appends new microbatches that shift alignment and we end up swapping kernels mid-request.
AJ: any chance the dispatcher handshake is the culprit (kernel launch/handshake overhead)?
Devon: dispatcher contributes ~8-12ms per switch. here's a small perf dump from pprof: 
```
fa_v2_fused   48ms/op (hot)
fa_paged      72ms/op (mem-bound)
dispatcher    10ms/op (handshake)
kernel-switch spikes 3.2x on p95
```
Maria: dispatcher handshake 10ms is higher than expected. did you try toggling kernel_prefetch or the new handshake batching?
Devon: toggled kernel_prefetch=false -> latency improved 4-6% but tail still bad. handshake batching reduced switch cost to ~6ms but paging path still heavier for small seq.
Sasha: hypothesis: paged tiled reducer kernel has poor L2 reuse at seq<=128 and microbatch<=4, so it becomes memory-bound vs the fused compute kernel. continuous batching can exacerbate because it forces mixed-semantics requests.
Devon: test patch: prefer fused on decode when microbatch<=4 AND kv_pages<=1 AND seq<=128. initial local runs: median -9%, p95 -18%. subtlety: need to ensure we don't regress quality when fused is quantized.
AJ: can you paste the router diff? I'll run a canary on T4 pool.
Devon: snippet: 
```diff
- if (policy == AUTO) choose_by_score();
+ if (policy == AUTO && stage == DECODE && microbatch_size <= 4 && kv_pages <= 1 && seq_len <= 128) prefer(FUSED);
+ else choose_by_score();
```
Maria: add a debug metric `router.pref_hint` emitted per request so we can tag rollouts in console and Grafana. also annotate why we preferred fused (microbatch/kv_pages/seq).
Sasha: also add a flag to force paged for diagnostic (router.force_paged) so we can A/B compare.
Devon: ran eval on 2k representative prompts with fused-prefer patch: no generation-quality regressions (perplexity identical within noise, 95% CI overlap).
Perf-bot: canary deploy started: pool=dedicated-gpu-3, build=sha:abc123, policy=prefer-fused-decode-smallbatches
AJ: canary results (2h): median latency -6.8%, p95 -15%, error rate same, throughput slightly up. kernel-switch metric down 72%.
Maria: great. rollout plan: step 10% every 30m, watch `router.pref_hint` and kernel-switch spikes; if kernel-switch > baseline*1.2 revert.
Devon: open question: should we implement sticky routing for session IDs to avoid mid-request flips when continuous-batching mixes prefill/decode semantics? pros: fewer switches; cons: less flexible autoscaling and possible load imbalance.
Sasha: sticky routing might help, but adds state and hurts binpacking. prefer short-term heuristics + metrics; revisit sticky if we see other cases.
Devon: agree. I'll push patch with router pref hint, feature flag, and perf dashboards. will follow up with graphs in ~2h :thumbsup:
AJ: thanks — I'll coordinate the canary steps and collect per-kernel flamegraphs.
Maria: tagging infra to keep an eye on GPU util and memfrag. :eyes:
Devon: uploading logs + pprof to the thread in ~30m. thanks all.
